title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - Common Law vs. Statutory Law
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: In the United States legal system, 'Common Law' is primarily created by:
options: Executive orders from the Governor or President
Precedents established by judicial rulings and court decisions
Administrative rules drafted by procurement officials
questions.explain: Common Law is derived from judicial decisions and custom (case law or precedents) rather than from statutes or constitutions enacted by legislative bodies.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When a direct conflict arises between an applicable Common Law precedent and a newly enacted Statutory Law regarding public procurement procedures, which takes precedence?
options: Common Law always supersedes Statutory Law.
The procurement director has discretion to choose.
The conflict must be resolved by federal arbitration.
questions.explain: Statutory Law (passed by a legislative body) takes precedence over Common Law. Statutes are often enacted specifically to overrule, modify, or clarify common law precedents.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which of the following is considered 'Statutory Law'?
options: A judge's ruling in a recent contract dispute.
The state's Public Procurement Code passed by the state legislature.
The traditions of purchasing recognized by the agency over the last 50 years.
An interpretation of a legal principle written in a law textbook.
questions.explain: Statutory laws are written laws enacted by a legislative body, such as a state's Public Procurement Code.
